output.summary: The ED rise is confined to admitted patients. Volume, admission rate, acuity and treat-and-release times are flat, which counts against volume and against ED nurse understaffing as the main cause. The rise began after the March 2026 hospitalist rounding change, which moved rounding to 09:30 and put new admissions first. That fits later discharges and longer boarding. Huddle and non-huddle days were comparable, supporting a causal reading of the discharge-timing link. Nurse strain and walkouts look like downstream effects of boarding. Inpatient capacity and the September bed-cleaning cut are unestablished. The best next step is to extend the early-discharge huddle and track it. Pausing the huddle or deferring case managers would harm the discharge flow.
